summary.headline: Jai Balaji Q1 FY27 revenue rose 24% YoY to INR1,683 crore; adjusted EBITDA up 46% to INR154 crore, PAT up 21% to INR85 crore.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 24% YoY to INR1,683 crore, with adjusted EBITDA up 46% to INR154 crore (about 9% margin) and PAT up 21% to INR85 crore (about 5% margin), attributed to price normalisation and operational efficiency. Ferroalloy and pig iron realisations rose sharply YoY, while DI pipe demand stayed subdued on slow government ordering and fund releases. Management declined to give volume or EBITDA guidance, citing uncertainty, but said pipe prices are at the bottom and cannot fall further. Expansion capex was revised up to INR1,112 crore from about INR1,000 crore, with completion expected by Q3 FY27 and the balance by end-2026.

financial_highlights.change: Net term debt was INR3,408 crore in FY21

segments.name: Ductile iron pipes (DI)
segments.commentary: About 15% of Q1 turnover; utilisation about 30% of the enhanced 5.5 lakh tpa capacity. Order book about four months at current dispatch rate. Management said pipe margins were similar to pig iron margins in Q1.

segments.name: Specialised ferroalloys
segments.commentary: About 27% of revenue; utilisation above 80% in the last quarter. Ferroalloy prices up 46% YoY. Management guided a long-term margin of 15-20%, and exports go to more than 42 countries.

segments.name: Pig iron
segments.commentary: About 19% of revenue; realisations up 16% YoY.

segments.name: TMT bars
segments.commentary: About 14.8% of revenue. Management expects West Bengal sales to rise to 50-70% of TMT volume from 15-20% previously.

segments.name: Commodity mix (sponge iron, billets, coke, scrap, fines)
segments.commentary: Sponge iron 7.4%, billets 3.5%, coke about 7%, scrap and fines about 1% of revenue. Sponge iron and billet realisations were broadly stable.

guidance_outlook: No volume guidance for DI pipes or ferroalloys for FY27; management said demand visibility is too uncertain.
No EBITDA-per-tonne guidance for pipes; management said prices are 25-30% below levels of a year and a half ago and 'cannot get worse'.
Ferroalloy utilisation expected at 80-90% once the new module is commissioned around December-January.
Management indicated revenue of INR7,000-7,500 crore in a normal market once expanded capacity is complete by end-2026; no FY28 or FY30 targets were given beyond this.
Post-monsoon recovery in DI dispatches and payments expected, with improvement from Q3 FY27.
capex_capacity: DI pipe capacity raised from 5 lakh tpa to 5.5 lakh tpa.

Specialised ferroalloy capacity rising to 1.9 lakh tpa from 1.66 lakh tpa; blast furnace to 7.5 lakh tpa from 6.3 lakh tpa; sinter to 12.08 lakh tpa from 9.08 lakh tpa. All expected commissioned by Q3 FY27.

Expansion outlay revised to INR1,112 crore from about INR1,000 crore (cause: equipment shipment delays, inflation, rupee depreciation, technical upgrades). About INR1,076 crore already spent, mostly from internal accruals; INR35-40 crore balance by end-2026.
Three railway sidings in operation; about 400 acres of land largely occupied for new capacity.
Management said the INR20 crore trial plastic-alternative pipe plant has sold no pipes and is in abeyance.
demand_pricing: Government DI pipe ordering is slow. Management said INR10,344 crore has been released by the Centre this year, and a FY26 backlog (only INR1,560 crore released in the budget) remains the constraint.
Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 extended to December 2028 with outlay of INR8.69 lakh crore (including INR3.5 lakh crore central assistance); AMRUT 2.0 also cited as a driver.
Competition intense while pipe utilisation stays at 25-35% industry-wide; management said intensity eases above 65-70% utilisation.
Jal Jeevan Mission receivables: management estimated 25-35% of outstanding dues collected, with the rest expected over the next 2-4 months.
Ferroalloy demand described as strong with repeat orders; management said 80-85% capacity is utilised.

qa_highlights.question: When will increased government spending translate into DI pipe dispatches?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a post-monsoon recovery in dispatches and payments, with improvement from Q3 FY27, after central fund releases and state matching shares.

qa_highlights.question: Will pricing pressure persist given competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Competition will persist until industry utilisation reaches 65-70%. Management said pipe prices are at rock bottom and Q1 pipe margins were similar to pig iron margins.

qa_highlights.question: Can you give DI pipe EBITDA per tonne guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management called pipe EBITDA guidance speculative given the 25-30% price fall and said it would reassess next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin profile of specialised ferroalloys versus conventional steel?
qa_highlights.answer: Conventional steel margins are 5-7%, specialised ferroalloys 15-18%. Long-term ferroalloy margin guidance is 15-20%, with a 1-2% swing from raw materials or freight.

qa_highlights.question: Why did capex rise to about INR1,100 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: The increase was about 7-8%, from delayed equipment shipments from China, inflation, higher freight, rupee depreciation, and technical upgrades.

qa_highlights.question: What is the DI pipe order book?
qa_highlights.answer: About four months at current dispatch rates. Q1 DI production was 41,000 tonnes, about 30-33% utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: What is current debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Repayable term debt is INR188 crore. Working capital is INR375-400 crore, sanctioned limits about INR525-550 crore, and net utilisation stays below INR500 crore with INR70-80 crore cash or unutilised limits.

risks_watch: Government fund releases and state payments: DI demand depends on clearing the FY26 backlog and recovering dues.
Pipe pricing at 25-30% below a year and a half ago, with management saying no further downside yet giving no guidance.
Capex overrun risk: budget rose to INR1,112 crore from about INR1,000 crore, and commissioning by Q3 FY27 depends on imported equipment.
Ferroalloy margins (15-20%) depend on raw material costs and freight; management said margins could move 1-2%.
Management did not give FY28 or FY30 capacity or profit targets; the INR7,000-7,500 crore revenue figure is conditional on a normal market.
key_quotes: So, as of now, we are not giving any projections, but definitely we are ready to encash it as the market progresses.
So, from here things cannot get worse, it has to improve.
Look, providing EBITDA guidance for the pipe business would be speculative at this stage, because prices have dropped by 25% to 30% compared to where they stood a year and a half ago.
So, the net utilization always remains below INR500 crores, while the sanctioned limit stays around INR550 crores.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term demand story (Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0, AMRUT 2.0) and on ferroalloy margins, but cautious and evasive on near-term DI pipe volumes, pricing and EBITDA per tonne, repeatedly declining to guide and saying it would be speculative. Defensive on the capex increase and on questions about the lack of top-line growth from past capex.
